technical_and_design_decisions: Target Spring Framework 6.x / Spring Boot 3.x on Java 17+ as stated in the specification.
Implement Kafka features as enhancements to the existing spring-kafka module using the standard KafkaListenerContainerFactory and ProducerFactory abstractions.
Implement Sqoop features as enhancements to spring-integration-sqoop, wrapping the Sqoop client and exposing its operations as Spring Integration messaging endpoints / operations.

Model configuration through @ConfigurationProperties classes so that the global options act as defaults while allowing per-deployment overrides via Spring property sources, profiles, or @Primary beans.
Use Testcontainers (KafkaContainer) and an embedded Sqoop harness for integration tests; use plain JUnit/Mockito for unit tests.
Adopt Spring Integration's request-reply abstractions (e.g., MessagingGateway, MessagingTemplate) for bindRequestor / bindReplier over Kafka, with reply topics and correlation ids for async replies.
Stream Sqoop logs by capturing Sqoop's stdout/stderr (Log4j appender) and forwarding them through a LogHandler / Commons Logging bridge into Spring's logging abstraction.
Implement Sqoop incremental loads by persisting the last-imported value (e.g., via a MetadataStore) and passing it as --last-value to subsequent runs.
For batching, switch the Kafka listener container to BatchMessageListener / batch-mode with configurable batch size, batch timeout, and a deserializer that supports Collection<Payload>.
For ACK modes, expose MANUAL / MANUAL_IMMEDIATE AckMode and route acknowledgement through Acknowledgment callback in the listener.
assumptions: A single, experienced Java/Spring developer performs all work; estimates are person-hours, not elapsed time.
The relevant base code (spring-kafka, spring-integration-sqoop) is already available in the workspace; no framework-wide refactor is required.
Test infrastructure (Testcontainers, Docker) is already available on CI; setting it up at the project level is the only effort counted.
An external Kafka broker and Sqoop server are available for acceptance / integration tests; spinning them up from scratch is not included.
Documentation means updating reference docs (Asciidoctor) and the relevant sample applications; no new website or marketing content is in scope.
All concurrency, compression, ACK, batching, and request-reply features are net-new in the targeted module; no migration of existing user code is required beyond documenting new options.
Sqoop log streaming does not require changes to the Sqoop binary itself; we only wrap and forward what Sqoop emits.

activities.activity_description: Review the existing spring-kafka and spring-integration-sqoop modules, design the new configuration model (defaults + per-deployment overrides), define the API surface for ACK, batching, bindRequestor, bindReplier, stop-job, log streaming, and incremental load, and produce a short design note.
Add Testcontainers-based KafkaContainer support, JUnit extension for starting/stopping the broker, base acceptance test classes, and wire them into the CI build configuration.
Expose concurrency / concurrency per-partition options on the KafkaListenerContainerFactory and corresponding @ConfigurationProperties, with validation and documentation.
Expose compression.type (none, gzip, snappy, lz4, zstd) on the ProducerFactory via @ConfigurationProperties and propagate it to the default producer config.

activities.activity_name: Kafka global configuration with per-deployment overrides
activities.activity_description: Design and implement the property hierarchy so the new defaults are picked up from spring.kafka.* but can be overridden by deployment-specific properties or beans (auto-configuration + @ConfigurationProperties).
Implement MANUAL / MANUAL_IMMEDIATE AckMode handling, expose Acknowledgment callback in the listener method signatures, and document synchronous vs. asynchronous ack semantics.

Implement a producer-side binding that publishes a request, waits for an async reply on a configured reply topic, and correlates the reply via KafkaHeaders.REPLY_TOPIC / CORRELATION_ID. Provide a gateway interface.

Implement a consumer-side binding that handles incoming requests from a requestor and asynchronously sends replies to the reply topic with the original correlation id, exposed as a Spring Integration endpoint.
Enable batch listener mode, expose batch-size, batch-timeout, and fetch-min-size properties, and provide a batch-aware message converter that produces Collection<Message<?>>.
Author an end-to-end acceptance test suite covering concurrency, compression, ACK, batching, bindRequestor and bindReplier scenarios, integrated into the CI Kafka build.
Expose a stopJob(...) operation on the Sqoop gateway that calls Sqoop's JobClient.stopJob(), propagates the status, and ensures resources are released (connection, JDBC handles).

Capture Sqoop logs (Log4j appender bridge over the Sqoop client process) and stream them into Spring's Commons Logging facade so they appear in the application log infrastructure. Provide a level / filter configuration.

Implement an incremental import mode (append / lastmodified) that reads the last successful value from a MetadataStore, passes --incremental and --last-value to Sqoop, and updates the store after a successful run.

Add JUnit/Mockito unit tests for all new Kafka and Sqoop components: configuration binding, factory wiring, ACK handling, batch conversion, request-reply correlation, stop job, log capture, and incremental state management.

Add integration tests against a real Kafka broker (Testcontainers) and a real Sqoop install validating: concurrency throughput, compressed payloads, MANUAL ack commits, request-reply round trips, batch ingestion, stop job cleanup, log streaming, and incremental loads with state persistence.
Update Asciidoctor reference docs, JavaDoc, and the sample applications (e.g., spring-kafka-sample, si-sqoop-sample) to demonstrate the new options, defaults, and overrides.
